- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ 0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast marginally, especially in early horizon.
- Overshoots after sharp upward moves (e.g., >70% spike) are common; apply downward correction by 5–10% in next 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, adjust downward; if below, adjust upward — especially when sentiment is neutral or mixed.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often overreact to short-term sentiment; dampen tail end if sentiment turns negative or flat.
- Lagged sentiment: if sentiment peaks 2–3 days prior, model may overreact; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days to match sentiment lag.
